items.prompt: Which of these is an igneous rock?
hints: It is made from cooled melted rock.
It is hard and often has sparkly crystals.
It is used for kitchen worktops.
items.explanation: Granite is an igneous rock.

items.prompt: Which of these is a sedimentary rock?
hints: It is made of pressed sand.
items.explanation: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of pressed sand.

items.prompt: A rock that forms from cooled melted rock is called ___.
hints: It begins with the letter i.
items.explanation: Igneous rocks form from cooled, melted rock.

items.prompt: What are fossils?

options.text: the remains or imprints of living things preserved in rock

items.explanation: Fossils are the preserved remains or imprints of living things that died long ago.

items.prompt: Which type of rock forms from layers of sand and mud pressed together?

options.why: Igneous rock forms from melted rock.
Metamorphic rock is changed by heat and pressure.

hints: It takes a very long time.
items.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment pressed together.

items.prompt: Marble is made when limestone is changed by heat and pressure. What kind of rock is marble?

options.why: Marble does not come from melted rock.
Marble is the changed form of limestone.

items.explanation: Marble is a metamorphic rock.

items.prompt: Sort each rock into the right group.
hints: Igneous rocks come from melted rock.
Sedimentary rocks are made of layers.
items.explanation: Granite and basalt are igneous, sandstone and limestone are sedimentary, and marble and slate are metamorphic.

items.prompt: Why are fossils not usually found in igneous rock?

options.text: The hot melted rock would destroy living remains.

hints: Igneous rock begins as melted rock.
items.explanation: Melted rock is too hot, so any living remains would be destroyed.

items.prompt: How can a fossil form?

options.text: An animal turns to stone while it is still alive.
A dead animal is buried quickly in sediment, which later hardens into rock.
A rock grows into the shape of an animal.
options.why: The shape comes from the animal.

hints: Over a long time it hardens.
items.explanation: Quick burial in sediment protects the remains, and over time the sediment becomes rock.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order for how a fossil forms.
items: The body is buried in mud or sand.
More layers build up and press down.
The sediment hardens into rock with a fossil inside.
hints: The rock is the last step.
items.explanation: A fossil forms after burial, pressure and hardening of the sediment.

items.prompt: Which description matches a metamorphic rock?

options.text: a rock formed from cooled lava
a rock changed by heat and pressure
a rock made of layers of sediment

hints: The rock was another rock first.
items.explanation: Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.

items.prompt: What is soil made of?

options.text: tiny pieces of broken rock and remains of living things

hints: Weathered rock makes up part of it.
It also has air and water.
items.explanation: Soil is made of broken rock, the remains of living things, water and air.

items.prompt: Which of these are made when rocks change in the rock cycle?

options.why: Fossils are not a rock type.

hints: The rock cycle makes new rocks.
items.explanation: In the rock cycle, rocks can be changed into sedimentary, metamorphic or igneous rock.

items.prompt: Rocks changed by heat and pressure are called ___ rocks.
items.explanation: Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.

items.prompt: In the rock cycle, what happens to a sedimentary rock that is buried very deep and heated?

options.text: It can become a metamorphic rock.

hints: There is a lot of pressure.
items.explanation: Heat and pressure can change a sedimentary rock into a metamorphic rock.

items.prompt: Which process in the rock cycle breaks rock into small pieces?
items.explanation: Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces.

items.prompt: A farmer finds that soil with a lot of clay holds water well but plants grow badly. Which is the best explanation?

options.text: The soil may hold too much water and have too little air.

hints: Water stays and air cannot get in.
items.explanation: Clay soil can stay too wet and has little air, which is poor for roots.

items.prompt: Adding rotted leaves and plant waste to soil usually makes it better for growing plants because it...

options.text: adds nutrients and helps the soil hold water

items.explanation: Compost adds nutrients and helps soil hold water, which supports plant growth.

items.prompt: Why do sedimentary rocks often show stripes or layers?

options.text: They form as layers of sediment build up over time.

options.why: The layers come from the sediment.

hints: Each layer was laid down at a different time.
Rivers drop mud and sand in layers.
The oldest layers are at the bottom.
items.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment, so they often show layers.

items.prompt: A scientist finds a fossil of a sea shell high on a mountain. What is the best conclusion?

options.text: The shell climbed up the mountain.
The rock was once under the sea.
The mountain is made of shells only.
options.why: It is made of sedimentary rock.

hints: Sea animals live in the sea.
Rock can be pushed up over time.
Sedimentary rock can form on the sea floor.
items.explanation: The rock formed at the bottom of the sea and was lifted up over a very long time.

items.prompt: Which of these takes the longest time?

options.text: the formation of a sedimentary rock from sediment

hints: Rocks form over millions of years.
items.explanation: Rocks form over very long periods of time, often millions of years.

items.prompt: True or false: Igneous rock forms when melted rock cools and hardens.
items.explanation: Magma or lava cools down and becomes solid, such as granite or basalt.

items.prompt: True or false: Sedimentary rock forms when rock is melted deep in the Earth.
items.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms from layers of sediment pressed together. Melted rock cools to form igneous rock.

items.prompt: True or false: Metamorphic rock is formed when heat and pressure change other rocks.
hints: What do heat and pressure do?
items.explanation: Limestone, for example, changes into marble.

items.prompt: True or false: Fossils are usually found in igneous rock.
items.explanation: The heat of igneous rock would destroy remains. Fossils are usually found in sedimentary rock.
